title: Training Persons with Spinal Cord Injury to Ambulate Using a Powered Exoskeleton
protocol: Perform a pre-screening evaluation with potential participants.
Briefly explain the details of the training process, including length of study, times per week, and hours per day.
Explain the known risks of participation, such as skin abrasions, potential injury from falling, and unforeseeable events.

Describe medical restrictions to potential participants regarding low bone mineral density at the hip or knee, recent fractures, inability to stand, weak upper extremity strength, and poor trunk control.
Review inclusion and exclusion criteria with the participant.
Encourage questions from the potential participant.
Address any concerns and answer all questions provided by the participant thoroughly.
Provide a detailed explanation of the study if prescreening is successful.
Initiate the screening process after providing a thorough explanation.
Perform a dual energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scan to evaluate bone mineral density bilaterally at the hip and knee.
Conduct an International Standards for Neurological Classification of SCI (ISNSCI) examination to assess injury level, motor function, and sensation.
Obtain a general medical history and physical evaluation which includes range of motion of the shoulders, hips, and knees.
Perform a skin check on areas of the lower extremity and lower back that contact the powered exoskeleton.
Exclude participants with hip and knee range of motion less than 20° flexion at either joint.
Ensure sufficient shoulder range of motion for proper crutch placement to perform sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit maneuvers.
Verify absence of pressure ulcers in areas contacting the exoskeleton.
Place the participant in a supine position.
Determine the pelvic width using a flexible tape measure and record it in centimeters.
Measure the upper leg length from the most prominent point of the greater trochanter of the hip to the knee joint line and record it in centimeters.
Repeat the measurement for the other upper leg length.
Record any limb length discrepancies.
Adjust the powered exoskeleton's center of the hip axis to the center of the knee axis according to the distance measured on each participant's upper leg lengths.
Measure the lower leg length from the knee joint line to the bottom of the foot and record it in centimeters.
Repeat the measurement for the other lower leg length.
Adjust the length from the bottom of the footplate to the center of the knee axis on the powered exoskeleton according to the distances measured for each participant's lower limbs.
Select a pelvic band by placing the participant in a seated position on a chair or bench with an open back.
Place the pelvic band closest in size to the participant’s pelvic width behind the person and slowly move it forward to test for fit.
Allow up to 1 cm clearance on either side of the pelvic girdle.
Affix the pelvic band to the thoracic uprights in the neutral or centered position after choosing the appropriate pelvic band size.
Adjust the fore/aft position of the pelvic band so that the trochanter is in line with the rotation of the hip joint when the participant is in standing position.
Fit and adjust the foot plate by removing the participant's shoe, removing the insole from the shoe, then placing the largest footplate possible into the shoe.
Place the insole on top of the footplate.
Adjust the dorsiflexion assistance of the footplate by fine-tuning the tension on the spring mechanism at the ankle.
Transfer into the device by placing one hand on the device and the other on their wheelchair.
Perform the transfer in one continuous motion if possible.
Rest momentarily on the upper "thigh" portion of the exoskeleton if unable to complete the transfer in one movement.
Resume the transfer with a second motion as needed.
Provide assistance with the transfer if necessary.
Sit properly in the device after transferring.
Place feet into the shoes.
Secure straps starting at the most distal point and moving proximally up the body, finishing with the chest straps.
Use the manual control feature to flex the hip slightly and extend the knee for easier foot placement.
Carefully guide the foot into the shoe, taking special care to ensure the toes are not curled.
Move the leg and foot back on the floor using the manual controls.
Fasten the shoe securely.
Follow the same steps for placing the second foot into the shoe.
Secure the straps directly below the knees.
Secure the straps above the knees.
Secure the straps for the upper thighs.
Take care to avoid crumpling of clothing beneath the straps to prevent unwanted friction and pressure points.
Secure the lower chest strap.
Secure the upper chest strap.
Examine the participant for any inappropriate contact, crumpled clothing or pressure points while seated.
Release the pressure by adjusting the fit and adding or removing padding as appropriate if a pressure point is identified.
Re-examine the fit after the participant stands up and walks a few steps.
Introduce the participant to the overall functions of the exoskeleton.
Explain the controller specific to the device.
Inform the participant about the goal of becoming independent with the exoskeleton.
Instruct that independence involves learning to control all functions of the device.
Note that there are short-term and long-term goals for independence.
Initially, have the trainer operate the controls to initiate desired movements.
Introduce the user to the device as early as possible during training.
Once comfortable in the device, allow the participant to take over the controls.
Equip the participant with a set of forearm crutches.
Instruct the participant to place the tips of the crutches posteriorly while seated.
Ensure that this positioning allows pushing weight over feet for standing maneuvers.
Note that crutches are necessary for all maneuvers including standing, walking, turning, and sitting.
Participants must use the exoskeleton with crutches at all times.
Explain the sit-to-stand procedure to the participant.
Have one trainer assist from behind the user.
Have another trainer guard from the front.
Instruct the participant to stand on their own and only use trainer assistance as needed.
Instruct the participant to place the crutches posteriorly.
Instruct the participant to lean forward while pushing off the crutches to assist standing after pressing the "Stand" command.
Encourage the user to concentrate on proper crutch placement initially.
Measure blood pressure after standing and periodically during the training session.
Ensure the participant demonstrates the ability to stand in "home" position using both crutches to maintain balance.
Place a mirror in front of the participant to provide visual feedback.
Instruct the participant to practice slight shifting of their weight laterally and posteriorly.
Have the participant understand the location and feel of the home position.
Instruct the participant to maintain balance with only one crutch.
Instruct the participant to lift one crutch off of the ground and hold that stance for up to 1 minute.
Instruct the participant to practice an additional one-handed balance exercise by lifting one crutch off the ground.
Have the participant perform this action while using the contralateral arm to reach over and touch the balancing arm's wrist.
Repeat these exercises to ensure the participant can perform maneuvers with either arm.
Teach the participant to weight shift laterally, allowing one foot to offload.
Instruct the user to lift their foot completely off the ground for 5 seconds.
Ask the participant to repeat this exercise by trying to offload with the other leg.
Instruct the participant to weight shift in anterior and posterior directions while properly placing crutches fore and aft.
Repeat exercises 5.2.2 to 5.2.5 five to ten times during the first session.
Continue practicing these exercises in subsequent sessions until the user feels comfortable.
Instruct the participant on how to walk with the powered exoskeleton.
Shift weight onto the left foot while unweighting the right foot using the controller.
Select the "Walk" mode on the controller.
Ask the participant to shift slightly forward towards a predetermined target.
Initiate the forward swing of the right leg.
Move crutches forward while simultaneously shifting weight forward and to the right after completing the swing with the right leg.
Step onto the right foot while unweighting the left foot.
Initiate forward swinging of the left leg upon sensing the participant's movement.
Repeat the forward crutching motion and weight shifting sequence for each leg consecutively to perform continuous walking.
Provide minimal assistance as needed during training sessions.
Grasp the powered exoskeleton or the participant to provide support if needed.
Correct the user on proper weight shifting while walking.
Have a second trainer provide assistance in an area of intact sensation, such as the shoulders, if necessary.
Incorporate different walking surfaces during training sessions, including carpet, concrete, asphalt, and grass.
Have the participant walk on surfaces with varying slopes such as up a ramp, down a ramp, over curb cutouts, and through uneven terrain.
Practice navigation of doorway thresholds, opening and closing swinging doors from both sides, and passing through automatic or revolving doors.
Incorporate activities such as reaching overhead into a cabinet and sitting on and standing up from a park bench.
Have the participant walk in a noisy environment while continuing to walk.
Have the participant stop on command during training sessions.
Ask the participant to stop after 6 min.
Use a dedicated trainer to spot the participant during the test.
Employ an additional trainer with a measuring wheel to determine distance covered.
Measure elapsed time using a stopwatch throughout the test.
Express the results of the 6MWT in meters walked over a 6-minute period.
Calculate average walking speed by dividing total meters walked by 360 seconds.
Identify and record the best 10 m time achieved during the 6MWT.
Place a chair behind the user when he or she is ready to sit.
Using the controller of the exoskeleton, place the exoskeleton in sit mode.
Introduce the user to the controller functions as early as possible during training.
Have the participant practice crutch placement posteriorly for balance maintenance over the chair after pressing the sit command.
Assist the participant with sitting movement, initially using two trainers and reducing to one trainer as skill improves.
Doff the device by releasing the straps starting with the chest and hip, progressing to the feet.
Remove the participant's feet from the device.
Encourage the participant to attempt transfer into their wheelchair on their own.
Provide assistance as needed during the transfer.
Inspect the participant's feet, lower extremities, and lower back for any bruising or abrasions once they are seated in the wheelchair.
Teach the participant to routinely check their lower extremities for signs of pressure points after completing walking sessions.
